method: The design is a rectangle measured in inches, and the stitched area is that rectangle multiplied by the filled coverage percentage, so a five by seven design at 40 percent covers 14 square inches. The estimated stitch count is the stitched area multiplied by the stitch density in stitches per square inch, rounded to the nearest whole stitch with an exact half rounded up, and a design that works out to less than one stitch is refused. Upper thread is the stitch count divided by 1,000 multiplied by the thread allowance in yards per 1,000 stitches, which is about 1 yard for 40 weight thread; bobbin thread is taken as one third of the upper thread. Thread is also shown in metres at 0.9144 metres per yard. The hoop or stabilizer minimum is the design plus the margin on every side, reported in inches and millimetres. Stitch-out time is the stitch count divided by machine speed in stitches per minute and is shown in minutes and seconds; it excludes trims, colour changes, rehooping and acceleration. Inputs are limited to a design from 0.1 to 24 inches per side, a density from 200 to 20,000 stitches per square inch, coverage from 1 to 100 percent, a thread allowance from 0.1 to 10 yards per 1,000 stitches, a machine speed from 100 to 2,000 stitches per minute and a hoop margin from 0 to 6 inches; text, negative numbers, scientific notation and out-of-range values are refused with the field named. Warnings appear for hoops larger than a common 200 by 300 millimetre maximum, densities outside 1,000 to 12,000 stitches per square inch, and runs over 500,000 stitches. The estimate assumes the density figure already includes underlay, and it does not model fabric, stabilizer, thread weight, design shape or stitch length. It runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Machine embroidery planning practice: filled areas are budgeted in stitches per square inch, with solid fills commonly running about 3,000 to 8,000 stitches per square inch.
Machine embroidery thread budgeting: upper thread is planned at roughly 1 yard of 40 weight thread per 1,000 stitches, and bobbin thread at about one third of the upper thread.
Machine embroidery hooping: the hoop and stabilizer must extend beyond the design on every side, and many home machines top out at a 200 by 300 millimetre hoop.
